root_traversal.ascent_cost: O(N) per ascent (re-walk via HashMap lookup)

in_struct_pointer.construction: eager Vec<NodeId> populated from parent list

hybrid_sidecar.construction: lazy: Vec<NodeId> materialised on first populate_from_walker call

rationale: hybrid_sidecar wins (or ties within noise) on every fixture: sheets 237.2 us vs in-struct 246.7 us (-3.8%); citm 1.847 ms vs 1.876 ms (-1.5%); tailwind 4.519 ms vs 4.658 ms (-3.0%).
root_traversal is 13x to 14x slower across the matrix and only justifies the bytes-per-node savings when ascent is essentially never invoked.

hybrid_sidecar carries the same 4 B/node footprint as in_struct_pointer once populated, but pays nothing if the consumer never calls populate_from_walker — preserving the option to skip ascent entirely on parse paths that never walk upward.
Ranking is monotonic in node count: the sidecar's amortised population cost dominates only on the smallest fixture, where the 9 us delta is well under the noise floor.
